scope.current_boundary: Teach elastic collisions, conservation of total kinetic energy, relative speed of approach equals relative speed of separation (u1 - u2 = v2 - v1), distinction between elastic and inelastic collisions (including completely inelastic coalescing collisions), solving simultaneous equations for unknown post-collision velocities, and the fundamental principle that total energy is always conserved even when kinetic energy decreases. Do not pre-teach Topic 4 forces, moments, or Topic 5 work/potential energy beyond the kinetic energy formula.

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Provides official assessment evidence for the 1-mark definition of elastic collision: total kinetic energy before equals total kinetic energy after.

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Illustrates direct application of relative speed of approach equals relative speed of separation to find post-collision velocity without requiring masses.

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Classic archetype: equal mass head-on elastic collision where moving incident particle comes to rest and stationary target moves off at original speed.

question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Equal masses exchange velocities: v_P = 0 and v_Q = v. Distractors show sharing speed (inelastic) or rebounding.

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Reinforces equal mass velocity exchange when both bodies have non-zero initial velocities.
